facts.fact: In March 1903 Tom Allen made a will at the Baptist hospital leaving the balance of his property to Tillie Hartgrove, with $10 each to his two sisters.
facts.conflict: date made: 4 March (202.c6, low; year cut off, hint says 24 March) vs the week before 3 April (200.c5, medium); witnesses (Marks, Newcomb, Brock) only in 202.c6 (low); the will was filed in probate court on 6 April 1903 (202.c5, 202.c7); Simon Bass filed it (202.c7) but refused to serve as executor (204.c1)

facts.fact: Allen's daughter, Mrs. Mary Taylor, was refused access to her father, and she took her case to attorney Frank A. C. MacManus, an old friend of her father, to gain access to him.
Gillespie tried to take Tom Allen's saloon from Murphy with a policeman's help, but the policeman refused to interfere and advised a warrant instead of an arrest.
Public Administrator Garrard Strode took charge of Tom Allen's estate in April 1903, which was in a muddled condition.
Friends of Tom Allen planned to apply to the probate court on 6 April 1903 for a conservator for him.
Gillespie said he had a claim against Tom Allen for goods sold to him.
On 6 April 1903 Mrs. Mary Taylor, Tom Allen's daughter, said she would apply to the courts that day to protect her father's property and would contest the will.
facts.conflict: name: Polly Taylor (1007.c7, medium, says she was cut off with $10 and will contest the will) vs Mrs. Mary Taylor (other claims); 202.c8 (medium) says she alleged the property was being dissipated by people with no right to it

facts.fact: Tillie Hartgrove had a writ of replevin issued at Clayton for a driving horse, and Constable Fred Lenz failed to replevin it on 21 April 1903.
facts.conflict: holder of the horse: William W. Heapes (211.c1, low, only source)

facts.fact: In May 1903 Circuit Judge Taylor refused Tillie Hartgrove a divorce from her husband, Martin Hartgrove, after learning she had been Tom Allen's housekeeper.
Tom Allen's estate had dwindled almost to nothing and was still in litigation in May 1903.
In July 1903 Allen's widow, who lives in England, demanded a dower interest in his estate, valued at $279.80, and engaged St. Louis attorney F. H. Sullivan to bring suit against the will.
In July 1903 Hartgrove and Gillespie left Clayton threatening to replevin a hat.
Public Administrator Garrard Strode filed the inventory of Tom Allen's estate in probate court on 28 July 1903, valuing the estate, including his saloon, at $279.80.
